REFERENCE ROLES: Reference 1 is the original story cover: preserve the man's lean ordinary adult silhouette, short tousled dark hair, angular face and muted grey practical work clothes, plus the excellent red wool coat and quilted lining. The cover supplies no precise close-up face, so keep a restrained early-middle-adult interpretation. Ignore all its scenery and typography. Reference 2 is the story's quarry landscape: use ONLY its Canadian Group of Seven-inspired connected colour/value masses, directional brushwork and cool slate-violet versus warm ochre relationships. Do not depict any quarry, rock or landscape. Reference 3 is the approved Sculpted Impasto folio: use its confident oil-paint materiality and clarity, adjusted to broad connected masses with quieter connecting passages. Do not copy its woman, armour, cape, medieval equipment, little landscape scenes or all-over chips.

KELRO'S IDENTITY: One lean human man, outwardly about 30-40 despite centuries of life, dark short untidy hair and same face/body in every study. Clean-shaven face, slim nose, ordinary subtly wary eyes expressed with opaque brush marks, no shiny eyes. Two arms, two legs, normal hands. His aliases Jalmot and Orvett are the SAME man, not separate identities. No permanent scars, no ear notch, no visible healing effect. No wound, blood, injury, corpse or death depiction.

CLOTHING AND MATERIALS: A roomy, practical, faded deep-red wool winter COAT with ordinary sleeves and front buttons, mid-thigh length as a restrained interpretation, visibly quilted lining. This is a working man's coat, not a cloak, cape, tunic, uniform or armour. A carefully repaired patch low on the hem. Muted slate-grey shirt layers beneath, charcoal brown trousers, worn mismatched leather boots; choose LEFT boot slightly too large and keep that side consistent in every view. The coat is cared for despite long use. Materials should be differentiated by paint direction and value masses: dense red wool, simple cloth, dull worn leather, matte skin. No ornate straps, weapons or invented jewelry.

"Kelro"
"A Busy Year for Dying"

Entire hair, hands and boots uncropped with generous ivory margins, no overlap. Concise labels: "Front", "Coatless", "Back".
On the right, two expressive head studies of exactly this man labelled "Wry" and "Guarded"; broad confidently painted facial planes, never a polished digital face. Below them, only three isolated personal costume studies labelled "Quilted lining", "Mended hem", "Battered hat". The open coat-lining study may show the small dark scorch mark beside its inner breast pocket. The battered hat is an ordinary muted brown cloth hat for his performance, not a wizard hat. A small five-stroke palette of red wool, slate, warm ochre, charcoal and ivory may sit at lower right without extra text.

PAINTING: Hand-painted Canadian Group of Seven-inspired oil. Large interlocking connected masses, decisive broad directional bristle strokes, selected substantial ridges of impasto on red wool, hair and major lit planes; allow calm matte connecting passages. Slight scraped edges and underpainting. Build the FACE with the same bold brush treatment as the body, readable through shape and value, without smoothing. Neutral warm light and rich cool shadows reveal materials; no sunset lighting or theatrical rimlight. Texture follows anatomy and cloth folds, never uniform surface flakes. No bevel-lit chips, mosaic facets, CGI modelling, glossy plastic, photographic face, anime, airbrush or hyperdetail.

STRICT CHARACTER-ONLY: Absolutely no location vignette, scenery, landscape, rooms, windows, floor or terrain patches under boots, rocks, plants, horizon, scenic backdrop, decorative prose, crowd, second person, stage screen or stage setting. Every study floats cleanly on uninterrupted warm ivory; no painted ground shadow or pedestal. No borders or panel boxes. Only the exact title/name and concise labels listed. Show the same coherent character from every view.
